items.label: 1. 法国防御古典变例（C11）
items.label_en: 1. French Defense, Classical Variation (C11)
items.explanation_en: White forms the e5-d4-c3 pawn chain and follows its direction with a kingside attack. The f4 advance supports e5, while Black counters by attacking the chain's base on d4 with ...c5. The game demonstrates how pawn structure can guide the attacking plan.

items.label: 2. 法国防御推进变例（C02）
items.label_en: 2. French Defense, Advance Variation (C02)
items.explanation_en: White advances e5 early to lock the pawn chain. Black's thematic ...c5 break attacks the base on d4, while White reinforces it with c3 and prepares queenside expansion with b4-b5. The locked structure directs both sides toward opposite-wing plans.

items.label: 3. 斯坦尼茨变例，攻击根部（C14）
items.label_en: 3. Attacking the Pawn-Chain Base (C14)
items.explanation_en: The e5-pawn is supported by both d4 and f4, so Black's ...c5 break attacks only one base and does not fully undermine the chain. White accepts the exchange and redirects play toward a kingside breakthrough with g4-g5, opening the g-file near Black's king.

items.label: 4. QGD少数兵突破（D36）
items.label_en: 4. Queen's Gambit Declined: Minority Attack (D36)
items.explanation_en: White's c4-d4-e3 chain points toward the queenside. White advances b4-b5 with a minority attack against Black's c6 pawn, creating a weakness on c5. The resulting outposts and piece activity show how the direction of a pawn chain can guide a queenside plan.

items.label: 5. 卡罗坎推进变例对比（B12）
items.label_en: 5. Caro-Kann Advance: Comparing Pawn Chains (B12)
items.explanation_en: The Caro-Kann's c6-d5 chain is sturdier than the French e6-d5 chain, but Black can still challenge White's d4 base with ...c5. White supports the chain, opens lines, and later advances f4 in the chain's direction. The comparison shows how pawn-chain structure changes weaknesses without changing the general counterattack principle.

items.label: 1. 弱格是怎么产生的（尼姆佐印度 E32）
items.label_en: 1. How Weak Squares Are Created (Nimzo-Indian)
items.explanation_en: Black exchanges the dark-squared bishop for White's knight. White avoids doubled pawns with Qxc3 and retains the bishop pair, but squares of the color of Black's missing bishop can become weak. The lesson is to evaluate the long-term color-complex consequences of an exchange.

items.label: 2. 象对弱色格的控制（后翼弃兵 D53）
items.label_en: 2. Bishops Controlling Weak Color Complexes (QGD)
items.explanation_en: White preserves the bishop on h4 while Black develops the bishop to b7 and applies pressure along the long diagonal. After dxc5, the d5-square loses its black pawn defender and may become a weak-square outpost. A bishop's color determines which color complex it can influence.

items.label: 3. 马占据弱格强格（国王印度 E91）
items.label_en: 3. A Knight Outpost on d5 (King's Indian)
items.explanation_en: White's d5 wedge creates weak squares, and Nxd5 establishes a knight outpost that Black's pawns cannot chase away. Black creates tactical complications with ...g5 and ...Nxe4, but after exchanges the knight remains on d5. A well-supported outpost can survive a tactical storm.

items.label: 4. 兵前进留下弱格（法国温纳瓦尔 C19）
items.label_en: 4. Pawn Advances Leave Weak Squares (French Winawer)
items.explanation_en: Black's exchange on c3 leaves White with doubled pawns and weak light squares, including d4. White's f4 advance supports the e5 wedge but also weakens f4 itself. The queen later helps defend d4 while targeting h7, illustrating that each pawn move can leave squares behind that need support.

items.label: 5. 利用d5弱格建立马的据点（尼姆佐印度 E43）
items.label_en: 5. Creating a Knight Outpost on d5 (Nimzo-Indian)
items.explanation_en: Black's ...c5 and ...d6 structure leaves d5 without a pawn defender. White accepts doubled c-pawns after Bxc3 in exchange for that weakness, then supports a knight maneuver with f3 and e4. Once e4 advances, White can route a knight to occupy d5. First create the weak square, then establish the outpost.

items.label: 1. 什么是半开放线（西西里防御 B20）
items.label_en: 1. What Is a Semi-Open File? (Sicilian Defense)
items.explanation_en: Black's ...c5 creates a semi-open c-file because Black has no pawns on it. After ...cxd4, the file opens fully, giving Black a natural route for a rook on c8. The example introduces the principle of placing a rook on a semi-open file to pressure the opponent.

items.label: 2. 争夺开放线的控制权（法国防御交换变 C01）
items.label_en: 2. Contesting an Open File (French Exchange Variation)
items.explanation_en: The central exchanges open the d-file, and both sides prepare to occupy it with a rook. White uses Re1 as part of a route toward d1, while Black contests the file directly. Open files should be claimed promptly because rook control brings the initiative.

items.label: 3. 双车叠压开放线（后翼弃兵 D30）
items.label_en: 3. Doubling Rooks on an Open File (Queen's Gambit)
items.explanation_en: White anticipates that the c-file will open and places a rook there with Rc1 before the exchange. After ...dxc4, White has a rook ready to occupy the file, then doubles the rooks to increase pressure. Predicting the pawn break makes the resulting rook placement more effective.

items.label: 4. d线争夺与车占中心格（国王印度 E61）
items.label_en: 4. Contesting the d-File and Occupying d4 (King's Indian)
items.explanation_en: After exchanges open the d-file, Black first establishes a knight on d4, then uses Rxd4 to bring a rook onto the central outpost. White contests the same file with a rook. The game shows how open files can transport heavy pieces to powerful central squares.

items.label: 5. 多线协同作战（西西里斯维什尼科夫 B33）
items.label_en: 5. Coordinating Pressure Across Multiple Files (Sveshnikov)
items.explanation_en: The Sveshnikov can produce activity on the c-, d-, and g-files. Each rook can be assigned a different route, creating pressure across the board rather than crowding one file. The lesson is to coordinate the rooks with the pawn structure and use every available open or semi-open file.

items.label: 1. 识别挤压信号：法国推进变中的坏象（C02）
items.label_en: 1. Recognizing a Cramped Position: French Advance
items.explanation_en: White's e5 wedge blocks Black's bishop on c8 and prevents the knight from developing naturally to f6. The forced knight detour and the contrast between White's active pieces and Black's immobile bishop reveal a space disadvantage. A bad bishop, awkward piece routes, and uneven development are key warning signs.

items.label: 2. 识别反击点：被压方的自救（卡罗-卡恩推进变 B12）
items.label_en: 2. Finding Counterplay from a Cramped Position (Caro-Kann)
items.explanation_en: Although White's e5 wedge restricts Black, the Caro-Kann bishop has already escaped to f5. Black challenges d4 with ...c5 and reroutes a knight toward g6, creating counterplay. A cramped side should identify pawn breaks and piece routes rather than defend passively.

items.label: 3. 子力拥挤可视化：活动格计数（国王印度 E94）
items.label_en: 3. Measuring Piece Mobility by Counting Squares (King's Indian)
items.explanation_en: White closes the center with d5, reducing Black's knights to a few useful squares while White reroutes a knight to d3. Counting available squares makes the space squeeze visible: White's knight has about six active options, while Black's knights have roughly three each.

items.label: 4. 空间优势的正确跟进：不能空转（法国古典变 C11）
items.label_en: 4. Converting Space with a Coordinated Plan (French Defense)
items.explanation_en: White follows the e5 wedge with f4, then coordinates Be3, Qd2, and queenside castling. Each move supports the same plan and prepares a kingside attack. Space is useful only when the pieces have targets and a clear way to exploit it.

items.label: 5. 弹簧效应：过度压缩被反扑（国王印度四兵进攻 E76）
items.label_en: 5. The Spring Effect: Counterattacking Overextension (King's Indian)
items.explanation_en: White advances four pawns to gain space but does not create a concrete attacking target. Black loads a counterattack with ...c5 and ...e6, opens the e-file, and targets the advanced center with ...Ng4. The deeper the space squeeze without a plan, the more dangerous the counterattack can become.
